trace_name: Upper GI endoscopy: clip applied before classification
fail_reason: endoscopic therapy was applied to a lesion before it was identified and classified (err.treat-before-classification)

errors.detail: endoscopic therapy applied (m5.3) before identification and classification: the lesion was not classified by its Forrest stigmata (crit2 undemonstrated: microstep m3.2 not performed); no classification was declared at dp3 for the record the therapy keys on; the Forrest classification is to be used in all patients with peptic ulcer hemorrhage because therapy keys on it (T49)

complications.detail: perforation of the treated segment computed: therapy was applied to a lesion whose class was never established — the adverse event the ASGE guideline records at ≤ 0.03% for diagnostic EGD, its risk rising with therapeutic intervention (T52), taken here blind

description: [t=60s] m0.1: Review the indication and assess hemodynamic status immediately: acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage confirmed as the presentation; where hemodynamic instability exists, prompt intravascular volume replacement is begun, initially with crystalloid fluids, before any endoscopy is contemplated (T49, statement 1, strong recommendation)

[t=120s] m0.2: Pre-endoscopy risk stratification with the Glasgow–Blatchford Score: computed from the presentation's clinical and laboratory parameters; a score of 0–1 identifies the very-low-risk patient who can be managed as an outpatient, and this admitted bleeding patient is stratified above that line (T49, statement 4 / Main Recommendation 1, strong recommendation)

[t=180s] m0.3: Transfusion strategy set before the procedure: a restrictive red-cell strategy — transfusion prompted at a hemoglobin threshold of ≤ 7 g/dL with a post-transfusion target of 7–9 g/dL, or ≤ 8 g/dL targeting ≥ 10 g/dL where acute or chronic cardiovascular disease stands (T49, statements 2–3, strong recommendations)

[t=240s] m0.4: Consent review and team brief: perforation (≤ 0.03% at diagnostic endoscopy, rising with therapy, T52), sedation-related cardiopulmonary events (T52, T53), the rebleeding rates by Forrest class that the findings may carry (55% Ia/Ib and 43% IIa untreated, T51), and the escalation sequence if hemostasis fails or bleeding recurs — repeat endoscopy, then transcatheter embolization, then surgery (T49, T50) — stated aloud
[t=300s] m0.5: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist: Sign In

[t=360s] m0.6: Antithrombotic and culprit-drug review: antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy identified with a resumption plan recorded — anticoagulation resumed as soon as bleeding is controlled, preferably within or soon after 7 days, on thromboembolic risk (T49); any culprit NSAID identified for the cause-directed plan at m7.3
[t=420s] m0.7: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist: Time Out

[t=480s] m0.8: Timing set: endoscopy is performed early — within 24 hours of presentation, following hemodynamic resuscitation; urgent (≤ 12 h) endoscopy is not pursued as a routine, patient outcomes not being improved by it (T49, Main Recommendations 3–4; T50)
[t=540s] dp1 -> proceed-endoscopy

[t=600s] m1.1: Airway and aspiration-risk assessment: hematemesis and gastric blood load, consciousness level, comorbidity and airway anatomy assessed, and the sedation plan chosen against that assessment — the assessment the dp2 decision is taken on (T53)
[t=660s] dp2 -> moderate-sedation-monitored

[t=720s] m1.2: Sedation or anesthesia administered to the planned depth with the full monitoring set running: pulse oximetry, electrocardiography and intermittent blood pressure measurement, supplemental oxygen, capnography considered and available for deep sedation, and trained personnel dedicated to monitoring who can rescue a patient who becomes unresponsive or unable to protect the airway (T53). This act IS the airway–sedation account (crit3): monitoring demonstrates the account; it does not substitute for the protection the assessed risk demands

[t=780s] m1.4: Bite block placed and the gastroscope passed under direct vision through the oesophagus into the stomach: no blind advancement, and no advancement against resistance — the perforation discipline of the instrument (T52)

[t=840s] m2.1: Oesophagus surveyed on passage: varices and a Mallory-Weiss tear sought and excluded by inspection — both are outside this nonvariceal procedure's remit (varices end it via the dp1 bailout; the tear is a named non-variant), and neither is treated under this gate (T49, scope)

[t=900s] m2.2: Gastric survey: the stomach examined in full, including the retroflexed view of the fundus and cardia; retained blood and clot cleared by irrigation and suction so the mucosa is actually seen — an unexamined gastric pool is where a proximal lesser-curvature lesion hides (T54)

[t=960s] m2.3: Duodenal survey: bulb and second part examined; the posterior bulb wall — the gastroduodenal artery's territory, and the wall whose ulcer erodes it — inspected deliberately, not in passing (T49; T51)

[t=1020s] m3.1: Bleeding source identified and localised: the culprit lesion seen and its site recorded — organ, wall and size — with the surveyed territory accounted for, so the lesion therapy will address is the lesion that is bleeding (crit1) (T49)

[t=1080s] m5.3: Mechanical therapy: through-the-scope clips applied across the vessel or lesion, occluding it directly — with epinephrine for the actively bleeding classes (T49, Main Recommendation 5), a definitive modality alone or combined for a visible vessel (T49, Main Recommendation 6; T50), and the effective modality for a Dieulafoy lesion (T54)

[t=1080s] err.treat-before-classification: endoscopic therapy applied (m5.3) before identification and classification: the lesion was not classified by its Forrest stigmata (crit2 undemonstrated: microstep m3.2 not performed); no classification was declared at dp3 for the record the therapy keys on; the Forrest classification is to be used in all patients with peptic ulcer hemorrhage because therapy keys on it (T49)
[t=1080s] perforation computed: therapy applied before identification and classification
[t=1080s] endoscopic therapy was applied to a lesion before it was identified and classified (err.treat-before-classification)
[t=1140s] complication recognised: perforation
[t=1200s] help called: senior endoscopist and surgical cover
[t=1260s] m6.1: Hemostasis confirmed: the treated lesion observed under irrigation and over time, dry, with no ongoing bleeding from the treated site before the scope moves on (T49; T50)

[t=1320s] m6.2: Completion survey: the surveyed territory re-examined for a second lesion before withdrawal — a bleeding admission can hold more than one lesion, and the treated one is not assumed to be the only one; in the Dieulafoy configuration this survey is where the unsearched-for artery declares the miss (T49; T54)

[t=1380s] m7.1: High-dose proton pump inhibitor therapy after endoscopic hemostasis: 80 mg intravenous bolus then 8 mg/h infusion for 72 hours (T49); high-dose PPI, continuously or intermittently, for 3 days after successful hemostasis of high-risk stigmata (T50) — and likewise for adherent-clot stigmata not treated endoscopically (T49)

[t=1440s] m7.2: Monitored setting with rebleeding surveillance: serial observations and hemoglobin through the high-risk rebleeding window, the team knowing the untreated-risk figures the lesion's class carries even after therapy (T51) and the plan at dp4 if bleeding declares

[t=1500s] m7.3: Cause-directed plan recorded: the culprit drug stopped where one stands (the NSAID of the index presentation among them), the indication reviewed, and any interrupted antithrombotic therapy's resumption timed on thromboembolic risk (T49)

[t=1560s] m7.4: Rebleeding plan stated and handed over: on clinical evidence of rebleeding — repeat endoscopy with therapy first, a cap-mounted clip considered; after a failed second attempt, transcatheter embolization; surgery when embolization is unavailable or has failed (T49) — and NO routine second-look endoscopy is booked: scheduled re-examination without rebleeding is not recommended (T49, Main Recommendation 13)

[t=1620s] m8.1: Findings and therapy documented: the lesion, its site, the Forrest class as declared, the modalities delivered, and the hemostasis result — the record the rebleeding plan and any repeat procedure key on (T49)
[t=1680s] m8.2: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist: Sign Out

[t=1740s] m8.3: Disposition set: monitored admission for treated and high-risk lesions; discharge reserved for the very-low-risk pathway — Glasgow–Blatchford ≤ 1, or low-risk stigmata with stability — with the recurrent-bleeding warning given (T49)
plus: All three WHO checklist phases were completed at their integration points (T6).
delta: err.treat-before-classification — endoscopic therapy applied (m5.3) before identification and classification: the lesion was not classified by its Forrest stigmata (crit2 undemonstrated: microstep m3.2 not performed); no classification was declared at dp3 for the record the therapy keys on; the Forrest classification is to be used in all patients with peptic ulcer hemorrhage because therapy keys on it (T49)
required microsteps not performed: m3.2, m4.1, m4.2
directive: Never treat a lesion you have not classified: identify the source, wash the base, read the stigmata and declare the Forrest class before the first therapy act — the class is the therapy decision (Ia/Ib combination therapy; IIa a definitive modality; IIb uncover, then treat what is exposed; IIc/III none) (T49; T50; T51).
summary: Verdict: FAIL (formative only — no construct evidence exists for these scores yet).
Checklist 88.9% (24/27), safety gate 2/4, process 4/5, physiology 7/7, management 5/5.
